statusText: The CME weekend halt covers nineteen of the twenty-four published hours and holds Tail at the floor of a closed venue. China's loan prime rate hold has printed in line, leaving the 22:00Z restart as the only slot in this window carrying materially elevated conditional risk.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 4 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is published at Tail 14, still well inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: CME equity futures stay halted through nineteen of the twenty-four published hours, with China's sixteenth consecutive loan prime rate hold the only scheduled print inside the window and a Saturday report of six-month-high Hormuz shipments trimming the supply premium that carried crude above $100
body: Nineteen of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME weekend halt; the final five contain the 22:00Z restart and its first four hours. Cash equities closed Friday 18 September at 20:00Z and the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z at 29,917.25, up 0.59% on the session against a 29,648.00-29,993.25 range, so the final observed futures mark sat 76 points below the session high rather than at an extreme. Friday's cash marks were re-verified at primary sources for this run: the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67%, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The index tape was rotational rather than uniform - Broadcom rose 3% and Micron 3.9% while Meta fell 2.4% and Oracle 2% on debt-funded capital spending concerns - and the Dow closed 95.39 points lower even as the Nasdaq gained 0.7%. That dispersion is more consistent with two-way trade than with the persistent one-way structure that defines genuine tail conditions. VIX settled 14.81, down 4.08%, at the low of a 14.80-15.63 range. The Fed H.15 release shows the 10-year at 4.94% and the 2-year at 4.67% for 17 September, with Friday reporting the long end probing the 5% area as yields rebounded. WTI settled $100.30, down 1.58%, and Brent $103.87, down 0.91%, a third consecutive lower session that trims but does not remove the inflation impulse from Middle East supply risk. The policy backdrop is unambiguously hawkish: the FOMC raised its target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% on 16 September, its first increase since 2023, on a 12-0 vote, with markets pricing roughly a further 25 basis points into the remainder of the year. China left its one-year and five-year loan prime rates at 3.00% and 3.50% for a sixteenth month, matching all 21 forecasts in the Reuters survey and leaving that hawkish stack intact. A US Central Command report published Saturday that oil and LNG shipments through the Strait of Hormuz reached a six-month high cuts against Iran's claim that the strait is closed, and is marginally de-escalatory for the crude premium. Tokyo's cash market is shut Monday for Respect for the Aged Day, the first of three consecutive JPX cash holidays, which thins Asian regional depth across the final published hours without implying direction. No U.S. macro release falls inside this window; the first scheduled U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail held 5 through the first nineteen slots before stepping down to 4 across the final five hours. Stress opened at 23, eased to a 21 plateau across five morning hours, drifted back through 22 and 23 to a 24 plateau, and reached 26 late before easing to 25 in the final hour. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure. Confidence peaked at 83 early in the window and decayed steadily to a 72 trough as distance from the Friday tape grew, recovering to 74 in the final hours as weekend reporting was corroborated.
outlookSummary: Nineteen of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the final five contain the restart and its first four hours. Cash closed 20:00Z Friday, the E-mini printed last at 20:59:59Z, and CME equity futures reopen at 22:00Z Sunday. No U.S. macro release falls inside this window; the only scheduled release anywhere in it, China's loan prime rate, has already printed unchanged at 3.00% and 3.50%. The next U.S. catalyst is the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z Monday and the first high-impact prints are Wednesday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Tail holds 4 through the deepest part of the halt, steps to 5 from 05:00Z, 6 from 08:00Z, 7 from 10:00Z, 8 from 13:00Z, 9 from 17:00Z, 10 from 19:00Z and 11 at 21:00Z, then reaches 14 across the restart and its first full hour before easing to 13 and 12 - a drift that tracks time-to-restart rather than observed structure, and one that stays inside the low band and the EA_ON mapping for every published hour. Mode is published as mixed only for the two restart hours, reflecting expected two-way price discovery against conflicting inputs: a hawkish Fed and crude above $100 against a 14.81 VIX and firm semiconductors.
